chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the slave girl, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Two divorces'.
ai.seo_question: How many divorces are required to fully divorce a female slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that a female slave (ama) requires only two divorces to be fully divorced, a ruling derived from the Quranic verse in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:229) which specifies 'two divorces' for slave women. This distinction highlights the jurisprudential nuance in Shia fiqh where the waiting period (iddah) and finality of divorce for slaves are simplified compared to free women, reflecting the specific legal status of slaves in classical Islamic law.
